content:
sarah.ops: heads up — thomas.p just forwarded me a suspicious 'Shared file access' email. says it asked to re-auth via a short link, clicked the link but didnt enter credentials. attaching header snippet and screenshot.

maria.sec: can you paste the full headers and the exact link? also which mailbox did it appear in (Gmail/Outlook)?

sarah.ops: pasted below — mail was in thomas.p@redwood.com (exchange). link in body was https://bit.ly/3xAbCdE

sarah.ops: ```From: "Shared Drive" <no-reply@goog1e.com>
Subject: Document shared with you
Received-SPF: softfail (domain of example.com does not designate 104.248.123.99 as permitted sender)
DKIM: none
Message-ID: <CAJf=xyz@mail.example.com>
X-Redwood-Client: Outlook-Web
``` 

eli.oncall: on it. resolving the bit.ly — gives hxxp://104.248.123.99/view?id=9876. spinning up sandbox scan on the page now. also checking exchange headers for other recipients.

sec-bot: sandbox: scan queued for https://bit.ly/3xAbCdE (job id sbx-9832)

sec-bot: sandbox: scan complete — MALICIOUS. detected credential harvester and JS that exfiltrates form POSTs to 104.248.123.99. screenshot attached.

maria.sec: thanks. immediate containment: block IP 104.248.123.99 at perimeter and add goog1e.com and the short link to MTA blocklist. IT, can you block and push rule?

it-helpdesk: will do now. blocking IP at firewall and creating transport rule to reject mail from domains matching *goog1e.*. also adding bit.ly redirect to deny list for safety. ETA ~5m.

it-helpdesk: done — firewall rule pushed and outbound/inbound MTA rule applied. noted in ticket #SEC-412.

sarah.ops: thomas says he clicked but didnt submit creds. can we confirm no OAuth approvals, no suspicious sessions?

eli.oncall: checked auth logs and OAuth audit — no new app approvals. revoking thomas.p's active sessions and refresh tokens as precaution. MFA still required. Also scanning login attempts from unusual IPs in last 24h.

eli.oncall: sessions revoked and refresh tokens rotated for thomas.p — manual step completed.

maria.sec: create IOC entry and incident record. Add these IOCs: 104.248.123.99, goog1e.com (homograph), https://bit.ly/3xAbCdE. Also add detection rule to flag similar subject lines and homograph domains.

sec-bot: IOC created: phish-2026-03-20-1852345678 (tags: phishing, credential-harvester, low-impact)

maria.sec: can we also search mail logs for messages with that subject or links to the short URL in the past 7 days? eli, can you run a mailbox search and provide list of recipients.

eli.oncall: running search now against exchange and spam quarantine. initial results: 3 deliveries (thomas.p, nina.pm, ops-oncall alias). quarantining the matching messages and notifying owners.

it-helpdesk: notified nina.pm and ops-oncall alias that message was malicious and removed from inboxes/quarantine. offered password reset if they clicked and submitted creds.

nina.pm (via thread): I did not click, thanks for the heads up.

maria.sec: recommend we also tighten DMARC to p=quarantine->p=reject and add a rule to flag single-character homograph domains (goog1e, go0gle, etc). I'll file a follow-up: SEC-413.

sarah.ops: can we run a quick check if any service accounts referenced in the email (attachments that call out to cloud storage) had their tokens used? KMS or service key touch?

eli.oncall: checked KMS and service-account audit logs — no key use or suspicious API calls stemming from that IP or URL. KMS unaffected.

maria.sec: good. proposed comms: short company-wide note from security + IT reminding about short-link checks and MFA. sarah, if you draft the copy we can send via #all-hands and email.

sarah.ops: draft ready, will post in 15m and request managers to remind teams. includes examples of homograph domains and how to inspect headers. cc: security training.

maria.sec: post-incident actions: 1) update phishing playbook with this homograph pattern and sandbox signature 2) add automated rule to block the specific bit.ly redirect pattern 3) escalate DMARC to p=reject for inbound vendor domains after testing 4) add IOC to company-wide blocklist 5) run phishing awareness micro-training next week.

it-helpdesk: completed forced password reset for thomas.p and sent guidance email with steps and contact. ticket SEC-412 updated.

eli.oncall: follow-up search completed — no other employee submitted credentials. closing active investigation unless new hits appear.

maria.sec: closing as low-impact incident. we'll track the post-incident follow-ups in SEC-413 and the training calendar. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sarah.ops: thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. I'll post the awareness message now and link the sandbox report and IOC.

sec-bot: incident updated: status=closed-low-impact, linked_ioc=phish-2026-03-20-1852345678, playbook_update=queued

maria.sec: assigning action items: eli — run homograph detection rule dev by EOD. it-helpdesk — coordinate DMARC change with infra next week. sarah — send comms and training invite. I'll draft the playbook entry.

eli.oncall: acknowledged. I'll share PR for detection rule in ~4hrs.

it-helpdesk: acknowledged.

sarah.ops: posted notice in #general and #security-alerts. included do/don't list and link to phishing report.

thomas.p: thanks folks. sorry for the noise, learned a lot from the flags you added.

maria.sec: nice work everyone. closing thread in 48h if no new hits.
